sections.overview: This Brazilian parrot is known from the central Amazon, between the lower Madeira and Xingu rivers.
sections.identification: It is distinguished by a bare, intensely orange head; the original description established it as a species rather than a young Vulturine Parrot.
sections.habitat: It is associated with humid tropical forest and tropical swamp forest in Brazil.
sections.diet: The selected sources do not provide enough species-specific detail to summarize its diet.
sections.behavior: Its flight shape and behavior are reported as very similar to those of its sister species, P. vulturina.
sections.reproduction: The Norwegian species account reports nesting in cavities.
sections.ecology: It is endemic to Brazil, with records from the Madeira–Tapajós interfluve eastward to the Xingu.
sections.conservation: The World Parrot Trust lists it as Near Threatened.
